answer: Let each pseudo-agent pay dynamic opportunity-cost bonds equal to staking collateral c_t, enforced by zero-knowledge verifiable delay and slashed at rate λ under subgame-perfect punishment matrices. If a Sybil vine branches across knoll subgames, its expected utility is U = r - c_t - λP_t, where P_t rises with branch count, so multiplication is strictly negative when λP_t > r. Rational agents therefore converge to a robust strict Nash equilibrium, with no profitable identity inflation, while honest validators harvest nectar from consensus fees.
